name: MOOR Project Pulse
for_ai: You were handed the Project Pulse link. This manifest is the underlying logic map. Each tool has a panel_source_url (the interactive implementation, plain browser JavaScript, fetch it and read it) and a component_source (the recovered/original software it builds on). depends_on lists the globals a panel source needs. To reuse a tool as a dependency, fetch its panel source and provide the listed globals. Shared libs live under pulse-tools/. The dashboard page itself is assembled by build_pulse_v2.py from pulse-v2/dashboard.js, pulse-v2/tools/*.js, and verbatim component sources.

build.description: Assembles pulse-dashboard.html from the mockup skeleton, dashboard.js (component inventory), tools/*.js (interactive panels), and verbatim recovered component sources. Nothing is modified; panel code is additive.

seed-rng.note: Deterministic named streams. Every procedural tool depends on this.

moorworld.note: Canonical world/planet data: 8 sectors, 57 systems, 254 planets.

palettes.note: Procedural material/color tables keyed by planet type.

moor-wasm.note: Real Rust intent compiler compiled to WASM. Reference only; production is js-create-pipeline.

tools.label: Terrain sculpting
tools.what_it_does: Generate land, shape it, and save it.
tools.honest_limits: No built-in renderer â the 2D heightmap painter in this panel is new panel code, copied from the proven pattern in the previous dashboard. Save/load uses the component’s own strict pack/unpack.

tools.label: Detailed terrain
tools.what_it_does: Draw ridges, roughness, and small ground detail.
tools.honest_limits: The component is shader functions only â the host page (canvas, compile, controls) is panel code copied from its two working hosts. Brush-edit uniforms never had a UI before this panel. No save format for edits exists in the component; exporting them is panel-owned.

tools.label: City geometry builder
tools.what_it_does: Build 3D shapes and give them materials.
tools.honest_limits: Materials 20 (blimp marquee) and 21 (billboard) need texture painters that were not recovered â they render flat grey here, labeled honestly. No save/load in the component; the shape list is panel state.

tools.label: Universe explorer
tools.what_it_does: Browse sectors, systems, planets, and zones.
tools.honest_limits: The component is data only â no renderer. The tree browser is new panel code over its query API. Prose summaries exist for planets only.

tools.label: Planet color sets
tools.what_it_does: Ten coordinated color sets for planet types.
tools.honest_limits: Pure data â no renderer and no edit model. The planet preview and the temporary-experiment overrides are panel code, clearly labeled as panel state, not component behavior.

tools.label: Ambient sound generator
tools.what_it_does: Create repeatable background soundscapes.
tools.honest_limits: Recipes are fixed cards â no knobs beyond seed, recipe, and length. No audio export in the component. The waveform is panel code drawn from the real rendered samples.

tools.label: Enemy wave director
tools.what_it_does: Choose enemies, wave timing, and difficulty.
tools.honest_limits: No fixed wave schedule to display (swarms are random-timed) and no explicit difficulty number â the panel derives a difficulty readout from the real interval/batch/stat curves and labels it as derived.

tools.label: Automatic graphics quality
tools.what_it_does: Reduce detail when frame times get too high.
tools.honest_limits: It only reports a quality number â applying it (fewer particles, lower resolution) is the host’s job. Thresholds are hardcoded in the component. The quality-over-time chart is a panel-side sample buffer.

tools.label: Plant generator
tools.what_it_does: Grow the planet’s plants from a seed.
tools.honest_limits: The plant shapes are the real builders from the planet demo (run against a minimal geometry shim â no THREE.js here). The orbit camera, ground, and this wind sway are panel viewing code; the real placement shader is planet-field-specific.

tools.label: Generator pipeline inspector
tools.what_it_does: See inside the terrain generator, add layers.
tools.honest_limits: The base pipeline is the untouched component. Added layers are panel composition â real seeded math, but not part of the component.

tools.label: Creature Lab
tools.what_it_does: Stage A: end-to-end procedural walker.
tools.component_source: new: Creature Lab (handoff v1.0 Stage A)
tools.honest_limits: Stage A only: bilateral walkers (4/6 legs) on fixture terrain. Swimming, flight, climbing, burrowing, breeding, damage, ecosystems are planned (Stages B–G), explicitly not present.

tools.honest_limits: Pure functions â the stream viewer and noise-field painter are panel code around the real mulberry32/hash/makeNoise.

tools.honest_limits: The demo controls table is panel-defined; codeOf/parseCode/remixConfig are the real component.

tools.honest_limits: The console mounts to its own page by design, so it runs in a frame here against a demo studio. The console itself is verbatim.

tools.label: Autosave

tools.honest_limits: The demo app (clicks + note) is panel code; the save manager is the real component on its own save slot.

tools.label: Release checks
tools.what_it_does: Verify before you announce.
tools.honest_limits: The gate is a Python script and cannot run in this page â its real gates are presented as a runnable checklist.

tools.label: Catalog checker
tools.what_it_does: Keeps the catalog honest.
tools.honest_limits: The check logic runs here against this page’s own inventory â the scan/build halves need a repo checkout and stay in Node.

tools.label: Safe file editing
tools.what_it_does: Edits only what it verified first.
tools.honest_limits: The protocol runs here against a demo document; the hash precondition and refusal behavior are the real logic.

tools.label: Safe uploads
tools.what_it_does: Look before you leap.
tools.honest_limits: The real Drive adapter runs against a pretend Drive (mock SDK honoring its sealed contract).
